newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end up on rumours of foreign limit rise.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end up on rumours of foreign limit rise.

text.p: Shares ended Friday's trading higher on rumours of an impending announcement on a rise in the foreign shareholders' ceiling, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose 7.12 points to 676.53. Advancing shares beat decliners 645 to 181, while an active 37.8 million shares changed hands.
"There were first rumours that an announcement would be made at 3.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), then it changed next week." a local broker said.
But other brokers discounted the market talk.
"On the surface, it appears that the rumours drove the market higher," said Chung Chang-shik of Dongsuh Securities.
"But this theory is weakly grounded, because the rise was fed by gains in individual shares."

Foreigners continued to actively sell KEPCO. The stock fell 700 won to 24,800. Brokers said they were selling the stock to reorganise portfolios before more stocks become available. The foreign shareholding ceiling is due to be lifted to 23 percent from the current 20 percent sometime this year, but no time has been set.
The finance ministry has denied the rumours.
Worries about labour strife evaporated after little action was seen despite a call for strikes by the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions.
